subtitle: A Gupta Princess, A Vakataka Throne, and the Copperplates of Power

panels.shot: low-angle medium close-up of a royal woman seated on a lion-legged throne, one hand resting on a copperplate, Deccan hills faint in the backdrop
panels.action: Prabhāvatīgupta sits in quiet command on the Vakataka throne, her Gupta-style crown catching the light as her fingers hover over an engraved copperplate beside a stylus.

dialogue.text: In the Deccan hills of Vidarbha, a Gupta princess signs copper, rules a Vakataka throne, and leaves us a question: was she regent, client, or queen in her own right?

i18n.hi: विदर्भ की दक्कन पहाड़ियों में गुप्त राजकुमारी ताम्रपत्र लिखती है, वाकाटक सिंहासन संभालती है, और सवाल छोड़ती है: वह अभिभावक थी, आश्रिता, या अपनी हक़दार रानी?

panels.shot: wide establishing shot over the Deccan plateau, with Nandivardhana’s fortified settlement and distant hills of Ramagiri
panels.action: The camera glides over the sunlit plateau of Vidarbha, past fields and scattered villages, towards the fortified town of Nandivardhana nestled near distant wooded hills.

dialogue.text: Late fourth-century Vidarbha. The Vakatakas rise in the Deccan, ruling from Nandivardhana and Ramagiri, their power balanced between plateau, forest, and old routes of trade.

i18n.hi: चौथी सदी के अंत का विदर्भ। दक्कन में वाकाटक उठते हैं, नंदिवर्धन और रामगिरि से राज चलते हैं, ताक़त पठार, जंगल और पुराने व्यापार मार्गों में बँटी है।

panels.shot: medium shot in an imagined Gupta court at Pataliputra/Ujjain, focused on a young princess listening intently, background blurred
panels.action: A younger Prabhāvatīgupta stands slightly behind a Gupta throne, her posture straight, eyes alert, taking in the measured rhythm of a royal assembly without speaking.

dialogue.text: In the north, Chandragupta II’s daughter Prabhāvatīgupta grows up in a Gupta court, where marriage is not only a rite, but a strategy that stitches kingdoms together.

i18n.hi: उत्तरी भारत में चंद्रगुप्त द्वितीय की बेटी प्रभावतिगुप्ता गुप्त दरबार में बड़ी होती है, जहाँ विवाह सिर्फ़ संस्कार नहीं, राज्यों को जोड़ने की चाल है।

panels.shot: ceremonial side-view shot of a marriage scene, with Prabhāvatīgupta and an unseen groom’s figure indicated by silhouette, focus on her face and garland
panels.action: In a ritual courtyard, Prabhāvatīgupta extends a garland towards a groom whose figure is half in shadow, symbolising Rudrasena II, as priests and elders look on from the edge of the frame.

dialogue.text: She is given in marriage to Rudrasena II of the Vakatakas. The copperplates will later remember this union as a knot binding Gupta prestige to Deccan ambition.

i18n.hi: उसे वाकाटक शासक रुद्रसेन द्वितीय से ब्याह दिया जाता है। बाद के ताम्रपत्र इसे गठबंधन कहते हैं, जो गुप्त गौरव को दक्कन की चाह से बाँधता है।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a Vakataka palace hall at Nandivardhana, Prabhāvatīgupta beside Rudrasena’s empty throne, courtiers in semi-shadow
panels.action: Within a pillared hall, an empty throne bears the lion motif of the Vakatakas while Prabhāvatīgupta stands at its side, listening to ministers, her expression watchful yet composed.

dialogue.text: In Nandivardhana, she learns a new court and a new land. Rudrasena II rules briefly, but inscriptions suggest his reign ends early, leaving sons too young for a throne.

i18n.hi: नंदिवर्धन में वह नया दरबार और नई धरती सीखती है। रुद्रसेन द्वितीय का राज छोटा रहता है, अभिलेख बताते हैं कि वह जल्दी चला गया, बेटे अभी सिंहासन के क़ाबिल नहीं थे।

panels.shot: dramatic medium close-up, Prabhāvatīgupta in mourning white, shadows lengthened, an empty space where a king once sat
panels.action: Prabhāvatīgupta, draped in plain white, stands in a shadowed hall, her gaze fixed on the vacant royal seat, while faint outlines of grieving courtiers recede into darkness.

dialogue.text: Rudrasena dies. The record falls silent on how, but the effect is clear: a Vakataka king is gone, minor princes remain, and the question of who will govern Vidarbha opens wide.

i18n.hi: रुद्रसेन मर जाता है। कैसे, अभिलेख नहीं कहते; बस इतना साफ़ है: वाकाटक राजा चला गया, किशोर राजकुमार बचे, और विदर्भ की सत्ता का सवाल खुला रह गया।

panels.shot: low-angle medium shot of Prabhāvatīgupta seated on a simpler regent’s throne, a child’s empty smaller seat beside her
panels.action: Prabhāvatīgupta sits on a slightly lowered throne, a smaller, vacant seat for a child heir placed close by, as ministers bow from a respectful distance, testing the new order.

dialogue.text: Some later scholars will call her regent, others see stronger power. Her own voice comes to us not in story but in copper, where she names herself mother of the crown prince and ruler.

i18n.hi: कुछ विद्वान उसे अभिभावक रानी कहते हैं, कुछ उसे और भी शक्तिशाली मानते हैं। उसकी अपनी आवाज़ कहानी में नहीं, तांबे में मिलती है, जहाँ वह खुद को युवराज की माँ और शासक कहती है।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of a copperplate on a low table, with intricate script, a stylus and Prabhāvatīgupta’s hand poised above
panels.action: A burnished copperplate lies on a low table, its incised letters catching the light as Prabhāvatīgupta’s hand hovers above it, fingers steady on the stylus before the first stroke.

dialogue.text: Her Poona copperplate, issued in her thirteenth regnal year, tells us how she wished to be seen: as Prabhāvatīgupta, of the Dharana gotra, daughter of the Gupta emperor, now granting land in her own right.

i18n.hi: उसका पूना ताम्रपत्र, उसके तेरहवें शासन वर्ष का, दिखाता है कि वह कैसी छवि चाहती थी: धारणा गोत्र की प्रभावतिगुप्ता, गुप्त सम्राट की बेटी, अब अपने नाम से भूमि बाँटती हुई।

panels.shot: medium shot over Prabhāvatīgupta’s shoulder as scribes sit cross-legged, one reciting, another incising letters onto copper
panels.action: Seated with calm authority, Prabhāvatīgupta listens while a court scribe chants the draft of a grant and another leans over the copperplate, carefully carving each syllable into the metal.

dialogue.text: “Write: born of Chandragupta, of Kuberanaga, mother of the Yuvarāja…”

i18n.hi: "लिखो: चंद्रगुप्त की पुत्री, कुबेरनागा की कन्या, युवराज की माता…"

panels.shot: split-focus medium shot, foreground on the word ‘Prabhāvatīgupta’ incised on copper, background showing Prabhāvatīgupta in profile
panels.action: The incised letters spelling ‘Prabhāvatīgupta’ run across the copperplate in the foreground, while in soft focus behind, her profile is turned slightly upward, serene yet resolute.

dialogue.text: Notice what her charter emphasises. It proclaims her Gupta lineage and Dharana gotra first, the Vakataka connection only implied through her sons and their future succession.

i18n.hi: देखो उसके दानपत्र में क्या सबसे पहले है। वह पहले अपना गुप्त वंश और धारणा गोत्र गिनती है; वाकाटक नाता बस बेटों और उनके होने वाले राज के ज़रिए झलकता है।

panels.shot: medium shot in a temple courtyard at Ramagiri, Prabhāvatīgupta offering flowers before an image of Narasimha
panels.action: In a stone-lined courtyard at Ramagiri, Prabhāvatīgupta stands before a fierce yet composed Narasimha image, offering a basket of flowers as priests look on from a respectful distance.

dialogue.text: The Ramtek Kevala-Narasimha inscription and Riddhapur plates echo her devotion. They present her as a Vaishnava queen, patron of Narasimha at Ramagiri, weaving faith into legitimacy.

i18n.hi: रामटेक के केवला-नरसिंह लेख और रिद्धपुर के ताम्रपत्र उसकी भक्ति दोहराते हैं। वे उसे वैष्णव रानी दिखाते हैं, रामगिरि के नरसिंह की संरक्षिका, जो विश्वास से वैधता बुनती है।

panels.shot: wide shot of Prabhāvatīgupta in an audience hall granting land to brahmanas, with countryside donors and recipients visible
panels.action: Prabhāvatīgupta sits in an audience hall as brahmanas from the countryside approach, holding palm-leaf petitions, while behind them glimpses of fields and village clusters suggest the land being granted.

dialogue.text: Her plates record grants of villages and fields to brahmanas. Through these formulae, her authority travels down to the soil, making abstract regency into practical rule over Vidarbha’s land and people.

i18n.hi: उसके ताम्रपत्र ब्राह्मणों को गाँव और खेत दान दर्ज करते हैं। इन विधानों से उसका अधिकार मिट्टी तक उतरता है, नाममात्र अभिभावकता को विदर्भ की धरती और लोगों पर असली राज बनाता है।

panels.shot: close-up of two hands clasping: a Vakataka minister’s ringed hand and Prabhāvatīgupta’s bangled hand
panels.action: A Vakataka minister’s hand, marked by a signet ring, meets Prabhāvatīgupta’s bangled hand in a firm clasp, with the blurred outlines of other officials suggesting cautious cooperation.

dialogue.text: Yet her regnal years are counted in Vakataka style, and her charters concern Vakataka territory. The administration remains Deccan in practice, even as Gupta blood runs at its centre.

i18n.hi: फिर भी उसके शासन वर्ष वाकाटक ढंग से गिने जाते हैं, और उसके दानपत्र वाकाटक भूमि के हैं। राज-व्यवस्था दक्कनी ही रहती है, भले ही बीच में गुप्त रक्त बहता हो।

panels.shot: medium shot of Prabhāvatīgupta in discussion with an imagined Gupta envoy, a map of India spread between them
panels.action: Prabhāvatīgupta and a northern envoy stand over a cloth map, one corner marked with Gupta symbols, another with Vakataka, as they point to Vidarbha and neighbouring regions in quiet debate.

dialogue.text: Were the Vakatakas now Gupta clients? Some historians read her emphasis on Gupta descent and Gupta marriages as proof. Others see a partnership: a Deccan kingdom aligning, not surrendering.

i18n.hi: क्या वाकाटक अब गुप्तों के आश्रित थे? कुछ इतिहासकार उसके गुप्त वंश और गुप्त विवाहों पर ज़ोर को सबूत मानते हैं; कुछ इसे साझेदारी मानते हैं: दक्कन राज्य जुड़ता है, झुकता नहीं।

panels.shot: low-angle wide shot of Prabhāvatīgupta addressing a court where young princes sit slightly behind her
panels.action: In a grand hall, Prabhāvatīgupta addresses assembled nobles while two young princes sit just behind her on smaller seats, their faces half-curious, half-solemn, watching their mother govern.

dialogue.text: “Until my sons come of age, the kingdom shall not falter.”

i18n.hi: "जब तक मेरे बेटे सयाने हों, राज डगमगाएगा नहीं।"

panels.shot: medium shot of an older Prabhāvatīgupta watching from a balcony as a grown prince mounts the throne below
panels.action: From a shaded balcony, an older Prabhāvatīgupta looks down, expression unreadable, as a grown prince moves towards the Vakataka throne amid ritual preparations in the hall below.

dialogue.text: Eventually her sons will sit fully on that throne. Later tradition will remember kings like Prithivisena I, but their ascent rests on the years when their mother held the realm together.

i18n.hi: आख़िर उसकी संताने पूरा सिंहासन संभालती हैं। परंपरा पृथ्वीसेन प्रथम जैसे राजाओं को याद रखती है, पर उनका उत्थान उन बरसों पर टिका है जब उनकी माँ ने राज्य जोड़े रखा।

panels.shot: close-up of a later copperplate being unearthed by modern archaeologists, Prabhāvatīgupta’s name half-covered by soil
panels.action: A modern hand brushes soil from an unearthed copperplate, revealing the incised name ‘Prabhāvatīgupta’ emerging slowly from the earth, letters sharp against the tarnished metal.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, her charters surface from the ground near Poona, Ramtek, and Riddhapur. Inscriptions, not epics, carry her voice from a time when queens seldom ruled in their own name.

i18n.hi: सदियाँ बीतने पर उसके ताम्रपत्र पूना, रामटेक और रिद्धपुर के पास की मिट्टी से निकलते हैं। महाकाव्य नहीं, अभिलेख उसकी आवाज़ लाते हैं, उस वक़्त से जब रानियाँ कम ही अपने नाम से राज करती थीं।

panels.shot: final contemplative medium close-up, Prabhāvatīgupta seated quietly with a rolled copperplate in her lap, background fading into abstract map-lines of Gupta and Vakataka realms
panels.action: Prabhāvatīgupta sits in stillness, a rolled copperplate resting across her lap, as faint, overlapping map-lines of the Gupta north and Vakataka Deccan glow behind her and then soften into darkness.

dialogue.text: Prabhāvatīgupta shows us a different face of power: a woman who held a Deccan kingdom through motherhood, marriage, and meticulous copperplates, leaving historians to debate labels while her signature endures.

i18n.hi: प्रभावतिगुप्ता हमें सत्ता की और शक्ल दिखाती है: एक स्त्री जिसने माँ, पत्नी और ताम्रपत्रों की बारीक़ी से दक्कन का राज्य थामे रखा, इतिहासकार नामों पर बहस करते रहे, उसकी दस्तख़त बची रही।

title_i18n.en: Prabhavatigupta Rules from the Vakataka Throne

subtitle_i18n.en: A Gupta Princess, A Vakataka Throne, and the Copperplates of Power
